thread:
deploy-bot: Proposing temporary MODEL pin: pin model-group 'text-quant' to artifact text-quant:v4-stable on hosted/dedicated pools for 2h (22:00-00:00 PT). Motivation: canary shows OOM / tail latency regressions after runtime v3.0.2 kernel reorder. Ticket INF-5321. Tagging @eng-runtime @ops.

caroline: Noted. Drop the canary snapshot and OOM counts pls — need to include in the advisory.

amir: Canary id canary-quant-20260528-9. Observed evictions/ooms on dedicated pool nodes: 12 OOMs in 20m, p99 latency from 820ms -> 1.9s. Median stable. Error-rate small but OOMs cause retries and higher tail.

tess: Is this a model-runtime compatibility (e.g., quant layout expectation) or purely runtime memory accounting? If model layout changed in build, pinning model helps while runtime team rolls a kernel fix.

amir: Root cause hypothesis: runtime v3.0.2 changed the allocator alignment which expands per-shard memory slightly on certain quantized kernels. text-quant:v4-stable was built against previous alignment and currently avoids the code-path that hits the allocator edge. Pining model->v4-stable should reduce memory pressure.

infra-bot: Actionable: deploy-bot can mark model-group pinned for selected pools. We can also enable telemetry tag X-Model-Pin=sticky. Recommend suppress autoscaling on affected pool for observation window to reduce noisy scale events.

ops-runner: I'll reserve the window and stand by for rollback. Runbook for rollback to unpinned behavior:
```
# remove model pin and allow model variants
curl -X POST https://models.internal/pins/text-quant/unpin -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN"
# if OOMs persist revert to runtime v3.0.1 on pool
kubectl -n inference set image ds/worker worker=redwood/runtime:v3.0.1 --selector=pool=dedicated-quant
# warmup cache and validate
./scripts/warmup_prefix_cache.sh --model text-quant:v4-stable
curl -f https://dedicated-quant.internal/health || echo "health failed"
```

caroline: Proposed guardrails: 1) if OOM rate >3 in 10m after pin, trigger rollback to runtime v3.0.1. 2) if p99 latency improves <10% vs pre-pin in 15m, unpin and escalate. Who owns telemetry?

amir: I'll own telemetry. Will wire an alert: alert if oom_count(dedicated-quant) >=3 in 10m or p99 >1.5x baseline for 10m.

tess: Add a short release-note entry and customer advisory: "Temporary model pin to text-quant:v4-stable to mitigate post-runtime v3.0.2 memory regressions; engineering investigating." I'll update docs.

infra-bot: Pin scheduled at 22:00 PT. Telemetry tag created: https://telemetry.internal/streams/text-quant-pin?c=canary-quant-20260528-9

deploy-bot: Pin action: model-group text-quant pinned to text-quant:v4-stable on hosted and dedicated-quant pools at 22:02 PT. Initial post-pin metrics: OOMs reduced to 1 in 10m, p99 down to 910ms. Monitoring.

ops-runner: Watching metrics in #eng-oncall. Suppressed autoscaling on dedicated-quant pool. Standing by to run rollback if alerts fire.

amir: After 20m post-pin: OOMs steady at 1, p99 = 885ms (improvement ~53% vs 1.9s). No error spike.

caroline: Good. We'll keep pin in place and schedule runtime patch (v3.0.3) next week with a regression test for allocator alignment. Follow-up: add an integration test in CI that runs quantized kernels with both alignments.

tess: Release-note snippet added to INF-5321 and PR created for customer advisory.

deploy-bot: Pin will auto-expire at 00:00 PT unless extended. If stable at 23:30 PT ops can unpin early.

amir: 23:32 PT update: stable, no new OOMs. ops, you can remove autoscale suppression and we can unpin at 23:45 if no regressions.

ops-runner: Unpin executed 23:46 PT: model-group allowed to float to latest variants. Post-unpin metrics: no new OOMs, p99 ~900ms. Closing INF-5321 with follow-up tasks: runtime patch and CI test. :white_check_mark:
